note: Players who spent all or most of their careers in Pittsburgh, plus coaches and owners, per the Pro Football Hall of Fame's team listing.
players: Won four Super Bowls and was MVP of two of them.
Immaculate Reception hero, Super Bowl IX MVP and the team's career rushing leader. His No. 32 is retired.
"The Bus" ran for 10,571 yards as a Steeler and retired after winning Super Bowl XL.
Bruising fullback who gave Pittsburgh its first 1,000-yard rushing seasons.
Did a bit of everything; named the league's MVP in 1946.
Acrobatic big-game receiver and Super Bowl X MVP.
Long touchdown catches in Super Bowls XIII and XIV; 8,723 receiving yards. Later became a part-owner.
Iron-man center who anchored the line for four Super Bowl winners.
Athletic center who followed Webster and was a Pro Bowl fixture in the 1990s.
Road-grading guard who led the run game in Super Bowl XL.
Guard who later coached the team in three separate stints.
"Mean Joe," Chuck Noll's first draft pick, was the cornerstone of the Steel Curtain. Twice Defensive Player of the Year; No. 75 is retired.
Tough, undersized lineman from the lean years. His No. 70 was the first number the team retired.
Smart, fast outside linebacker with 32 career interceptions.
Fierce middle linebacker; Defensive Player of the Year in 1976.
Pass rusher who led the NFL in sacks in 1994 and helped reach Super Bowl XXX.
Team-record 57 interceptions; so physical that the league changed its pass-coverage rules in 1978.
Ballhawk with 52 interceptions, second in team history.
1993 Defensive Player of the Year and the team leader in punt- and kick-return yards.
Instinctive, game-changing safety; 2010 Defensive Player of the Year with two Super Bowl rings.
builders: Founded the team in 1933 and ran it for more than five decades.
Led the team through its glory years; the league's Rooney Rule is named for him.
Built the 1970s dynasty through the draft and won four Super Bowls.
Made the playoffs in 10 of 15 seasons and won Super Bowl XL.
Pioneering scout who found stars at historically Black colleges, including John Stallworth and Donnie Shell.
others: Also in the Hall with shorter Steelers stints: Johnny Blood, Cal Hubbard, Bobby Layne, Marion Motley, Johnny Unitas (cut as a rookie in 1955), Len Dawson, Jim Finks, Bert Bell, Tony Dungy, Dick LeBeau, Russ Grimm and Mike Munchak.
greats: Two Super Bowl wins and the team leader in passing yards (64,088) and touchdowns (418).
Super Bowl XL MVP and the team's career leader in catches (1,000) and receiving yards (12,083).
Steel Curtain end with 78 sacks, fourth in team history.
Undrafted pass rusher, 2008 Defensive Player of the Year and author of the 100-yard Super Bowl interception return.
Dependable tight end with 592 catches, third in team history.
Longtime defensive leader, second in team history with 92 sacks through 2025.
Team sacks leader (115 through 2025), tied the NFL single-season record with 22.5 in 2021, and 2021 Defensive Player of the Year.
retired: Retired numbers: 70 (Ernie Stautner), 75 (Joe Greene) and 32 (Franco Harris).
